gantt-chart-excel-maker: Choose Website launch, Event plan, Home renovation or Exam preparation to see a ready example, then type your own project name. Pick your region so dates and paper size match how you write them.

Paste your tasks from a sheet or upload a CSV or Excel file. Give each task a start and an end date, or a start date and a number of days. The tool shows what it read, so you can check the dates before anything is made.

The preview shows your timeline as it will look in Excel: green for the part that is done, light orange for what is left, red for late tasks and a yellow column for today. Choose days for a short project or weeks for a long one.

Save the Excel file and open it. Change a date or a percent done and the bars, status and totals follow. The Owners sheet shows how many tasks each person has, how many are done and how many are late.
attendance-register-excel-maker: Pick Office, Shop, School staff or Workers. This sets the days off and how many months to include. Then type your organisation name and choose the first month and year.
Tick the days of the week that are off, and type your holidays, one a line, with the date first. These are greyed on every month sheet. Choose an alert percentage so low attendance turns red.
Paste your names or upload a CSV or Excel file. A name column is needed and an ID column is optional. The tool shows what it read. If you add nothing, the file has empty rows ready to type in.

Open the file, and for each person and day pick a code from the drop-down: present, absent, leave or half day. The columns on the right and the Summary sheet add up days worked, leave and attendance percentage.
invoice-excel-template-maker: Pick Freelancer, Shop, Services or Quotation. This sets the title, the number of lines and a starting note. Type your business name, address and contact details.

Type up to three taxes, such as VAT or Sales tax, and the rate for each. Leave them empty if you do not charge tax. The tool does not know your tax rules, so the names and rates are exactly what you type.
Paste or upload your price list and your customer list, or skip this and type them in the file. The invoice then fills the price from the item you pick and the address from the customer you pick.

Open the Excel file, choose a customer, pick items and type quantities. Print the Invoice sheet or save it as a PDF, then add the invoice to the Invoice Log to see who has paid, who owes and who is late.
delivery-bill-excel-maker: Choose Milk, Tiffin, Newspaper or Water cans, then type your business name, the unit and the month. Pick your region so money and dates look right.

Paste your customers or upload a CSV or Excel file with a name column. Phone, price per unit, usual quantity per day and last month's balance are optional. For anything missing, the tool uses the price and quantity you type.

The preview shows every customer with the usual quantity filled in for every day. Days that differ show in orange, and a day with nothing delivered shows in red. Paid and pending customers get their own colours.
Download and use it every day

Open the Excel file and change only the days that were different. Type what each customer paid. Use the Bills sheet to print one customer's bill and the Reminders sheet to open WhatsApp with a message ready for customers who still owe.
stock-register-excel-maker: Choose Shop or kirana, Kitchen or cafe, or Office or stationery to see ready item lists, then type your business name. Pick your region so money and dates match how you write them.

Paste your items from a sheet or upload a CSV or Excel file. A name is needed. Unit, opening stock, reorder level, cost and selling price are optional. The tool shows what it read, so you can check before anything is made.
The preview shows the sheets: Items, Stock Log, Stock, Order List and Summary. Choose With sample data to see stock moving, or Blank to start clean.
Download the .xlsx. On the Stock Log sheet add one row for every purchase, sale or adjustment. Stock updates, low items turn red and the Order List shows what to buy.
credit-ledger-excel-maker: Choose Shop or kirana, Wholesale or trade, or Services or tuition, type your business name and the credit period in days that you allow.
Paste your customers or upload a CSV or Excel file. A name is needed. Phone, opening balance, credit limit and a note are optional. Choose With sample data to see it filled in.
The preview shows Customers, Entries, Balances, Statement and Summary. Balances shows what each person owes and how old it is.
Download the .xlsx. On the Entries sheet add a row each time you give credit or receive a payment. Use the WhatsApp link on the Balances sheet to send a reminder to anyone who is overdue.
timesheet-excel-maker: Type the normal hours in a day and the overtime multiplier you use, for example 1.5. These are your own rules, so use the numbers from your agreement.
Paste your people or upload a CSV or Excel file. A name is needed. Role and hourly rate are optional. Choose With sample data to see two weeks logged.
The preview shows People, Time Log and Totals. Each shift shows hours, overtime and pay.
Download the .xlsx. On the Time Log add a row for each shift: the date, the person, start, end and any break. Totals shows hours, overtime hours and pay for each person.
fees-rent-tracker-excel-maker: Choose Tuition or school fees, Rent, or Society or gym, or type your own word such as Fee. It is used in headings and in the reminder message.
Paste your list or upload a CSV or Excel file. A name is needed. Phone, class or flat, monthly amount and opening balance are optional.
The preview shows People, Tracker, Pending, Receipt and Summary. The tracker has a column for each of twelve months.
Download the .xlsx. In the Tracker type the amount paid in each month. Pending shows who owes what, with a WhatsApp link for a reminder. Receipt prints a receipt for one payment.
daily-cash-book-excel-maker: Choose Shop, Freelancer or service, or Home business to see sample income and expense categories, then type your business name.
Type up to four modes such as Cash, Bank, UPI, and the balance in each at the start, separated by commas.
The preview shows Lists, Cash Book, Month and Year. The Cash Book shows a running balance for each mode.
Download the .xlsx. Add a row for each receipt or payment with the mode and category. Month and Year show income, expenses and what is left.
budget-planner-excel-maker: Choose Household, Student or Small business to see sample income and spending lines, and name your budget.
Paste your income and spending lines or upload a CSV or Excel file. Each row needs a kind (income or expense) and a name. A planned amount per month is optional.
The preview shows Settings, Budget and Summary. The Budget has a plan and an actual column for each month.
Download the .xlsx. Each month type what you actually earned and spent. The Summary shows left over, percent saved and charts.
supplier-payment-tracker-excel-maker: Type the default credit days and how many days before the due date you want a warning. Use the days from your own agreements.
Paste your suppliers or upload a CSV or Excel file. A name is needed. Phone, credit days and a note are optional.
The preview shows Suppliers, Bills, Totals and Summary. Each bill shows its due date and status.
Download the .xlsx. Add a row for every bill and type the amount and date when you pay. Overdue bills turn red and due-soon bills turn yellow.

ganttExcelGuide.title: Gantt Chart Excel Maker: Project Timeline from Your Task List (Free)
ganttExcelGuide.subtitle: Make an Excel Gantt chart from your own tasks. Bars, the today column, late tasks and totals fill in by themselves. Free, nothing uploaded.
faq: Is the Gantt Chart Excel Maker free?
Yes. It is free, with no sign-up and no limit on how many workbooks you make. The file is built on your own device.
How does the Gantt chart work without macros?

Each cell of the timeline has a colour rule that compares the date at the top of its column with the start and end dates of its row and with the percent done. When you change a date, the rule runs again and the bar moves. Because there are no macros, the file opens without a security warning and works in other spreadsheet apps.
What should my task list look like?

One task on each row, with a heading in the first row. A task name is needed. Start and end dates are best, or a start date and a number of days. Owner and percent done are optional. The tool matches your headings, shows what it read and lets you pick a column yourself if it guessed wrong.
Will it open in Google Sheets or WPS Office?

The workbook uses common formulas and colour rules that Excel, Google Sheets, WPS Office and LibreOffice all understand. Colours and column widths can look a little different from one app to another, so look over the Plan sheet the first time you open it.
How does it decide a task is late?

A task is late when its end date is before today and it is not 100 percent done. Today is read from your computer when you open the file, so the status and the yellow today column stay up to date by themselves.
Can I switch between days and weeks?

Yes. Pick Days or Weeks above the timeline inside the file, and change the date it starts on to move through time. You can also choose a unit before you download, or let the tool pick one from the length of your project.
Can I add more tasks later?

Yes. Empty rows are kept under your tasks, and you choose how many. Type new tasks in them and the bars and totals include them. If you need more rows than you kept, make the workbook again with more spare rows and paste your tasks in.
Is my task list uploaded or saved on a server?

No. The tasks, the dates and the workbook stay on your device, and {{siteName}} does not receive them. Your settings are remembered in this browser only, and your list is never saved. Start again clears everything.

attendanceExcelGuide.title: Attendance Register Excel Maker: Monthly Sheets for Your Staff (Free)
attendanceExcelGuide.subtitle: Make an Excel attendance register for your own staff, months, days off and holidays. Pick a code for each day and the totals fill in. Free, nothing uploaded.
faq: Is the Attendance Register Excel Maker free?
Yes. It is free, with no sign-up and no limit on how many registers you make. The file is built on your own device.
How do the weekends and holidays work?

You tick the weekly days off and list your holidays once. Every month sheet then greys those days and leaves them out of the working-day count, so the attendance percentage is based on the days people were expected to work.
What do the codes mean?

The default codes are P for present, A for absent, L for leave and HD for half day, which counts as half present. You can rename the codes on the Settings sheet. Each day is a drop-down, so entries stay consistent and the totals are correct.
Can I make a register for a whole year?
Yes. Choose 12 months and the workbook has one sheet for each month plus a Summary sheet. Names are typed once on the first month and appear on the others.
How is the attendance percentage worked out?

Days present, with half days counted as half, divided by the working days in the month. Working days are the days that are not a day off or a holiday. The limit that turns a percentage red is a number you choose, and it is only a colour, not a rule.
Will it work in Google Sheets or WPS Office?

The workbook uses common formulas, drop-downs and colour rules that Excel, Google Sheets, WPS Office and LibreOffice all understand. Open one month sheet first and check the colours and drop-downs in your app.
Can I reuse a month sheet for another month?
Yes. Change the month cell at the top of the sheet and the days, weekdays, weekends and holidays update. Clear the old codes first, because the entries stay where they are.
Is my staff list uploaded or saved on a server?

No. The names, the register and the workbook stay on your device, and {{siteName}} does not receive them. Your settings are remembered in this browser only, and your list is never saved. Start again clears everything.

invoiceExcelGuide.title: Invoice Excel Template Maker: Printable Invoice with Your Own Taxes (Free)
invoiceExcelGuide.subtitle: Make an Excel invoice that fills prices and addresses from your lists, adds your own taxes and keeps an invoice log. Free, nothing uploaded.
faq: Is the Invoice Excel Template Maker free?
Yes. It is free, with no sign-up, no watermark on your invoices and no limit on how many templates you make. The file is built on your own device.
Does it know my country's tax rules?

No. You type the name of each tax and its rate, and the invoice adds them to the subtotal. Check your own rules for what to charge, how to number invoices and what to print on them. Rates and rules change, so nothing is built in.
How does the price fill in?
Pick an item in a line and its price is looked up from the Items sheet. You can type over the price for one invoice, and you can type an item that is not in the list. A discount column is optional.
Can it print on A4 or Letter?
Yes. Choose your region and the paper size is set for you. The Invoice sheet is set to fit one page wide, so you can print it or save it as a PDF from Excel.
How does the Invoice Log work?

Add one line for each invoice you send, with the number, date, customer and amount. Type what was paid and the due date. The log works out the balance and marks each invoice Paid, Part paid, Unpaid or Late, and shows the totals and a chart.
Does it write the amount in words?
No. It adds up the lines, the taxes and any shipping, and can round the total. Amount in words is not included, so write it in by hand if your documents need it.
Will it work in Google Sheets or WPS Office?
The workbook uses common formulas and drop-downs that Excel, Google Sheets, WPS Office and LibreOffice all understand. Check the Invoice sheet in your app the first time, especially the print layout.
Are my customers and prices uploaded or saved on a server?

No. The lists and the workbook stay on your device, and {{siteName}} does not receive them. Your settings are remembered in this browser only, and your lists are never saved. Start again clears everything.

deliveryBillExcelGuide.title: Monthly Delivery Bill Excel Maker: Milk, Tiffin, Newspaper and Water Can (Free)
deliveryBillExcelGuide.subtitle: Make an Excel sheet for milk, tiffin, newspaper or water-can bills. Usual quantities are pre-filled, bills and reminders are worked out. Free, nothing uploaded.
faq: Is the Monthly Delivery Bill Excel Maker free?
Yes. It is free, with no sign-up and no limit on how many workbooks you make. The file is built on your own device.
Who is this for?

Anyone who delivers the same thing regularly and bills once a month: milk and tiffin sellers, newspaper and magazine agents, water can suppliers, laundry and cleaning rounds, and meal prep. Set the product and unit and everything else follows.
Why is every day already filled in?

Most days a customer takes the same amount, so the sheet fills each day with their usual quantity. You only change the days that were different. Different days turn orange and days with nothing delivered turn red, which makes mistakes easy to spot.
How are the bills worked out?

Total units for the month multiplied by the price per unit, plus any opening balance from last month, minus what the customer paid. The status shows Paid, Part paid or Pending. Prices are whatever you type for each customer.
How do the WhatsApp reminders work?

The Reminders sheet shows a Send reminder link for each customer who owes money and has a phone number. Clicking it opens WhatsApp with a message ready, and you press send yourself. The file never sends anything. Use a phone number with no spaces, and set the country code in the region settings.
How do I do next month?
Make a new workbook for the new month and put last month's balance in the opening balance column. You can also upload your customer list again, with the balances, so nothing needs to be typed twice.
Will it work in Google Sheets or WPS Office?

The workbook uses common formulas, drop-downs and colour rules that Excel, Google Sheets, WPS Office and LibreOffice all understand. Open the Entry and Reminders sheets in your app first and check that the colours and links work.
Is my customer list uploaded or saved on a server?

No. The names, phone numbers, balances and the workbook stay on your device, and {{siteName}} does not receive them. Your settings are remembered in this browser only, and your list is never saved. Start again clears everything.

stockExcelGuide.subtitle: Make a stock register in Excel with reorder alerts, an order list and stock value. Add your items, log stock in and out. Free, nothing uploaded.

How do I record stock coming in and going out?

Open the Stock Log sheet and add a row for each movement: the date, the item from a drop-down, whether it came in or went out, and the quantity. The Stock sheet adds everything up for you, so you never type the current stock yourself.
How does the reorder alert work?

You type a reorder level for each item. When the current stock falls to that level or below, the status on the Stock sheet changes to Order now (or Out of stock) and the item appears on the Order List. The level is only the number you type, so set it from how fast you sell and how long suppliers take.
What is the Order List?

A sheet that picks out every item at or below its reorder level and shows how much to order. The suggested quantity is a multiple of the reorder level that you choose in Settings, with an estimated cost, and you can order a different quantity.
Can it show the value of my stock?

Yes, if you type a cost for each item. The Stock sheet multiplies current stock by cost, and the Summary shows the total value and the number of items that are low or out. Sale price gives the value of your stock at selling prices too.
How many items and log rows can I use?
You choose spare rows for new items and the number of log rows when you make the file. The defaults suit a small shop and can be raised under More options.
Does it work in Google Sheets, WPS Office and without macros?

The workbook uses common formulas, drop-down lists and colour rules that Excel, Google Sheets, WPS Office and LibreOffice understand. There are no macros, so it opens without a security warning. How do I record credit and payments?
On the Entries sheet add a row with the date, the customer from a drop-down, whether it is credit given or a payment received, the amount and a note. Balances and the statement update by themselves.
What do the ageing columns mean?
They split what a customer owes by how old it is, in steps of the credit period you typed. Payments are counted against the oldest credit first, so the older columns shrink before the newer ones.
How does the WhatsApp reminder work?

Each customer with a phone number gets a link on the Balances sheet. Tapping it opens WhatsApp with your message already filled in with their name and amount. You press send yourself. Nothing is sent from the file.
What is the credit limit for?

If you type a limit for a customer, the status shows a warning when their balance goes over it. It is only the number you type, so decide the limit from how much you are willing to risk with each person.
Can I print a statement for one customer?
Yes. Pick the customer on the Statement sheet and it lists their entries with a running balance, ready to print or save as a PDF.

faq: Is the Timesheet Excel Maker free?
Yes. It is free, with no sign-up and no limit on how many workbooks you make. The file is built on your own device.
How are hours and overtime worked out?

Hours are the end time minus the start time minus any break (in minutes). Hours up to the normal hours you typed are regular and hours above are overtime. Overnight shifts are handled when the end time is earlier than the start.
How is pay worked out?

Regular hours are paid at the hourly rate you typed for the person. Overtime hours are paid at that rate times the multiplier you typed. The tool does not know any wage rules, so use the figures from your own agreement.
Can I use it without hourly rates?
Yes. Leave the rates empty and you still get days, hours and overtime for each person. Pay is only worked out for people who have a rate.
Can I see a total for each person?
Yes. The Totals sheet adds up days, regular hours, overtime hours and pay for each person for the period you set in Settings.
How many shifts can it hold?
You choose the number of log rows when you make the file. The default suits a small team for a few months and can be raised under More options.

sections.heading: What a Gantt chart in Excel is for
paragraphs: A Gantt chart lays your tasks out against a calendar, so you can see what starts when, what overlaps and what is running late. Many people want one in Excel because they already have the program and can change a date without learning new software.
This tool makes the workbook for you. You give it the tasks and dates, and it builds a sheet with a timeline that colours itself, a status for every task and a summary for each person.

sections.heading: Choosing days or weeks, and keeping dates clean
paragraphs: Use days for projects of a few weeks, where each column is one day and weekends are shaded. Use weeks for longer projects, where each column is a week and the whole plan fits on a screen. You can change this inside the file.

Dates are the part that most often goes wrong. Keep one date format in your list, check the What we read panel before you make the file, and look at the Plan sheet once to confirm the bars sit where you expect.

sections.heading: Private, and what to check
paragraphs: Everything is made on your device, so your task list is never uploaded. The workbook has no macros and no links to the internet.
Late and done are worked out only from the dates and percentages you type. Review the plan with your team before you rely on it.

sections.heading: What the register does
paragraphs: An attendance register records, for each person and each day, whether they were present, absent, on leave or worked half a day. This tool builds that register as an Excel workbook, with a sheet for every month and a summary across months.
You decide the people, the months, the weekly days off and the holidays. The workbook then greys the days off for you and adds up each person's days.

sections.heading: Setting it up so the numbers are right
paragraphs: Fill in the Settings sheet first, because every month follows it. List all holidays, including ones that fall on a day off, and choose which weekdays are off. Type each person's name once, on the first month.
Use the drop-down in every cell rather than typing, so codes stay the same. Leave days off blank, as they are already greyed and are not counted.

sections.heading: Private, and what to check
paragraphs: Everything is made on your device, so your list of names is never uploaded. The workbook has no macros and does not connect to the internet.
The register only counts what you enter. Leave rules, pay rules and attendance limits are your own, so check any totals against your policies before you use them for pay.

sections.heading: What the invoice workbook does
paragraphs: This tool builds an invoice as an Excel workbook that does the sums for you. It has a printable Invoice sheet, an Items sheet for your prices, a Customers sheet for your addresses and an Invoice Log that tracks payments.
Pick a customer and the address appears. Pick an item and the price appears. Type a quantity and the line, the taxes and the total are worked out.

sections.heading: Setting up taxes and numbering
paragraphs: You choose up to three taxes and type each rate yourself. This keeps the workbook usable in any country and for any kind of tax. It also means you are responsible for the right names and rates.
The invoice number is a plain box you can change, so use whatever numbering your business follows. Keep one running list in the Invoice Log so numbers are not repeated.

sections.heading: Private, and what to check
paragraphs: Everything is made on your device, so your customer and price lists are never uploaded. The workbook has no macros and does not connect to the internet.
Check a few invoices by hand before you send them, including the taxes and the rounding. This tool is not an accounting or tax program, and the totals are only as correct as the rates you type.

sections.heading: Why a pre-filled sheet saves time
paragraphs: A blank grid of customers and days takes a long time to fill in each month. Most customers take the same amount every day, so this workbook fills in their usual quantity for you. You only touch the days that were different, such as a holiday or a double order.
The totals, the amount, the balance and the status are worked out automatically, and a printable bill for each customer is on its own sheet.

sections.heading: Keeping balances and reminders tidy
paragraphs: Type last month's unpaid amount as the opening balance, and what each customer pays in the Paid column. The balance then shows what is still owed, and the status shows who is paid, part paid or pending.
The Reminders sheet gives each customer who owes money a link that opens WhatsApp with a polite message ready. You read it, and you press send.

sections.heading: Private, and what to check
paragraphs: Everything is made on your device, so your customer names, phone numbers and balances are never uploaded. The workbook has no macros and does not connect to the internet.
Check one or two bills by hand before you hand them out. Prices and quantities are only what you type, so make sure they match what you agreed with each customer.

sections.heading: Why a stock register still matters
paragraphs: Running out of a fast-selling item costs sales, and stock that sits on the shelf ties up money. A stock register tells you which is which, without a paid inventory app.
This tool builds the register for you. You list the items once, log every purchase and sale, and the workbook works out the current stock, the value and what is running low.

sections.heading: Setting reorder levels
paragraphs: A reorder level is the stock at which you should order again. A common way to think of it is the number you sell in the time a supplier takes to deliver, plus a small cushion. Only you know your own sales and delivery times, so the tool never guesses a level.
Review the levels every few months. Items that sell faster than before need a higher level.

sections.heading: Private, and what to check
paragraphs: Everything is made on your device, so your items and prices are never uploaded. The workbook has no macros and no links to the internet.
Stock is worked out only from the movements you log, so a missed entry will show as a wrong count. Do a physical count now and then and fix the log.

sections.heading: What a credit ledger is for
paragraphs: Many shops and small businesses sell on credit and keep the account in a notebook. A ledger in Excel does the same job, but adds up balances, shows who is overdue and finds an old entry in seconds.
This tool builds the workbook. You add customers once, record each credit and payment, and the sheets show every balance, how old it is and who to remind.

sections.heading: Keeping credit under control
paragraphs: Overdue credit is easier to collect when you ask early and politely. The ageing columns show how long each amount has been waiting, so you know whom to call first.
Set a credit limit for people you are not sure about, and look at the limit status when you are about to give more.

sections.heading: Private, and what to check
paragraphs: Everything is made on your device, so customer names, phone numbers and balances are never uploaded. The workbook has no macros.
Balances are only as correct as the entries you make. Agree the balance with the customer if there is any doubt.

sections.heading: Why track hours in a sheet
paragraphs: Hourly work, shifts and overtime are easy to get wrong when added up by hand. A timesheet that does the sums gives the same answer every time and is easy to show to the person being paid.
This tool builds the timesheet for you with your own normal hours, overtime multiplier and rates.

sections.heading: Getting the times right
paragraphs: Type times in the same way for every row, such as 9:00 and 18:30. Enter the break in minutes. For night shifts the end time can be earlier than the start and the tool will count past midnight.
Look at the first few rows after you enter them to be sure the hours match what you expect.

sections.heading: Private, and what to check
paragraphs: Everything is made on your device, so names, hours and pay are never uploaded. The workbook has no macros.
Pay rules differ by place and agreement, and the tool does not apply any. Check the totals against your own rules before paying anyone.

sections.heading: Collecting the same amount every month
paragraphs: Schools, landlords and societies collect a fixed amount from many people each month. A simple tracker shows who has paid, who has not, and how much is pending.
This tool builds that tracker. You list the people and the monthly amount, and the sheets add up the rest.

sections.heading: Reminding politely
paragraphs: Most late payments are forgetfulness. A short polite message with the amount works better than a long one. The reminder link fills in the name and amount, and you can change the wording before you build the file.
Keep a receipt for every payment so there is no argument later.

sections.heading: Private, and what to check
paragraphs: Everything is made on your device, so names, phone numbers and payments are never uploaded. The workbook has no macros.
Amounts are only what you type. Check totals against your bank or cash before you rely on them.

sections.heading: A cash book is the simplest set of accounts
paragraphs: Writing down every rupee that comes in and goes out, each day, is the base of almost all small-business accounting. A cash book in Excel makes the sums automatic.
This tool builds a cash book with your payment modes and categories, plus monthly and yearly summaries.

sections.heading: Keeping it up to date
paragraphs: It is easier to log at the end of each day than to catch up at the end of the month. Keep bills and UPI screenshots until you have entered them.
Compare the balance for each mode with your actual cash and bank balance now and then.

sections.heading: Private, and what to check
paragraphs: Everything is made on your device, so your income and expenses are never uploaded. The workbook has no macros.
This is a record of money you type, not tax or accounting advice. Check with a professional where it matters.

sections.heading: Why plan before you spend
paragraphs: A budget turns vague worry about money into numbers. Planning what you expect to earn and spend, and comparing it with what happens, shows where money goes.
This tool builds a budget with your own lines for a full year.

sections.heading: Making a plan you can keep
paragraphs: Start from your real last few months, not from what you wish you spent. Put fixed items such as rent first, then variable ones. Leave a line for things you did not expect.
Look at the actual column once a month and adjust the plan.

sections.heading: Private, and what to check
paragraphs: Everything is made on your device, so your income and spending are never uploaded. The workbook has no macros.
The figures are only what you type. This is a planning aid, not financial advice.

sections.heading: Paying suppliers on time
paragraphs: Buying on credit helps cash flow, but missed due dates can cost goodwill or discounts. A tracker that shows what is due soon helps you plan cash.
This tool builds the tracker with your own credit days.

sections.heading: Credit days and due dates
paragraphs: Credit days are what you agree with each supplier. The tool never assumes them. Set a default, and give a supplier or a single bill its own days where it differs.
Check the due dates against the supplier's own bill.

sections.heading: Private, and what to check
paragraphs: Everything is made on your device, so supplier names and amounts are never uploaded. The workbook has no macros.
Amounts and dates are only what you type. Check against your supplier statements.
